# CANDIDATE: NAMED_LEVEL_SWEEP_RETEST

**Filed:** 2026-07-09
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)
**Type:** new_trigger
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

Price often sweeps a named level (e.g., prior day high) to trigger stop‑losses, then returns to test that level as support/resistance; entering on the retest after a sweep captures the mean‑reversion bounce. This two‑step pattern (sweep then retest) is distinct from existing strategies that enter on the sweep alone or wait for a second touch without a sweep condition.

## Mechanism

Define a named level (prior day high for longs, prior day low for shorts). If price penetrates the level by >0.1% (sweep) and then closes back inside the level on the next bar with volume > average, go long (for high) or short (for low) at the close of the retest candle. Exit: stop just beyond the sweep extreme (beyond the wick that caused the sweep); target 1R or exit when price moves 0.5% beyond the level in the direction of the trade. Regime filter: only active between 10:30‑14:00 ET when VIX is between 12‑20; avoid first/last 30 minutes.
